question: During India's independence movement, who was the only President of the Indian National Congress who resigned from the presidency even after being elected?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhash Chandra Bose.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During India's independence movement,** Subhash Chandra Bose **was the only President of the Indian National Congress who resigned from the presidency even after being elected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian National Congress (INC) chose Subhas Chandra Bose as its President in 1938.
 
• In 1939, he ran for re-election to the party's presidency.
 
• Gandhi was a strong supporter of Pattabhi Sitaramayya for President. Bose was re-elected as president of the INC, however, thanks to the support of radical factions inside the party.
 
• Gandhi was dissatisfied with his re-election and claimed that Pattabhi Sitaramayya's failure was his own.
 
• Thirteen members of the Congress Working Committee resigned in protest over Gandhi's suffering.
 
• Several delegates who had previously supported Bose began to endorse Gandhi at this time.
 
• Bose resigned from the presidency in 1939 because it was getting increasingly difficult for him to work as Congress President.
 
• When Subhash Chandra Bose resigned from the Presidentship of the Indian National Congress, the seat was offered to Dr. Rajendra Prasad.__
 
• He became a member of the Indian National Congress in 1911 when the annual session was held in Calcutta.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent president of the Constituent Assembly on 11th December 1946.
